observed.frontend: success with empty diagnostics for the exact selected file/import cut
observed.interpretation: Five corrected/control cases plus two ExpectedBad old-transition witnesses. Seven passing declarations are not seven safety passes.

review.source_semantics: Separate actual canonical claude-opus-5-5 review: APPROVE_SCOPED_SOURCE with M1-M7 qualifications
review.actual_data: Separate GPT-based mechanical review: consistent for the scoped observed result; no new semantic or security verdict

M1.meaning: The five corrected/control cases and the two ExpectedBad cases have different meanings. Each ExpectedBad declaration succeeds when its selected old transition reaches an unsafe state; they are bad-old reachable witnesses, not safety passes.

M2.premise: The model records failure state and first code atomically. This corresponds only to the selected T20/T21 schedules in which refusal is recorded before the parked read is released.
M2.schedules: T20 observe/bind refusals are synchronous, and the reprove rejection is awaited before release. T21 awaits the second route rejection before release.
M2.excluded: Real async entry refusals can latch a microtask later. This result establishes no global synchronous-latching theorem. General step interleavings, simulation, invariant runs and exhaustive checks are outside this adopted result; delayed-latch and consumer go-gate work remains separate.

M3.premise: The baseReturn guard assumes the base provider settles only after its own route call settles and propagates route rejection. The selected test behavior is evidence for its fixture schedule, not a proof of the unsupplied production provider implementation.

M4.omission: The model does not track the provider promise rejection-code oracle. A rejected route is expected to propagate STATE_CHANGED in the implementation, whereas model baseReturn uses NoRouteCapture after a prior rej has already recorded the original first code. NoRouteCapture therefore does not become first in the selected traces.
M4.counts: The T20 zero codec and sealed-getter counts are only partly represented by later observation refusal; exact counts and the provider rejection-code oracle are not established by this model.

collapsed_or_omitted_paths: inner.prove throwing, including ERR_B4_UNEXPECTED or an inner LinkError
base provider resolving without invoking the route: baseReturn is disabled while route 1 remains Out
M5.other_abstractions: Lookup resolution, valid binding/preimage hashes, codec and observing segments, and foreign reentry inside collapsed segments are premises or outside scope.

M6.membership: Only the seven named Test-suffixed declarations are selected. toPreimage and toProofRead are unselected prefix runs; the latter expectation is exercised through cases built on it. Including the two prefix runs would be a different nine-declaration selection, not this result.
M6.sampling: Seed 1, one example per selected declaration; no broad sampling or exhaustive coverage is claimed.

M7.mixed_prefix: oldT20LeavesFailedExpectedBadTest uses the corrected route-entry/after-preimage prefix, which sets claimed and checks okAt, before the unchecked old after-proof transition. This is a mixed-prefix witness, not pure OLD02 replay.
M7.justification_and_limit: On that selected prefix the old entry and unchecked after-preimage take the same branches; the old after-proof transition reads neither claimed nor first. Other old callback, provider-prove and sealed-observation behavior is assumed equal to the current version; the source comparison supplied only the affected old route and wrappers.

evidence_boundary: The retained selected captures support the frontend and five-plus-two result. Historical pre/post pin and lifetime observations remain owner attestations; independent current hash agreement does not reconstruct historical process or filesystem behavior. No stronger closure theorem is inferred.
